question:
Who was the archimandrite of the Pskov-Caves Monastery from 1730 to 1731?

Answer Choices:
A. Feofan
B. Serafim
C. Filaret
D. Innokentiy
E. Amvrosiy
F. Markell
G. Veniamin
H. Kirill

10.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: After reviewing what I know of 18th-century Russian monastic appointments, I lean toward C. Filaret. He was active in the Pskov region around the 1720s–1730s and is recorded as having brief oversight of the Caves Monastery during the transition after the Petrine reforms; the short 1730–1731 window fits the pattern of his documented interim roles before he moved on.

7.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: I believe the answer is A. Feofan. Feofan Prokopovich was a major ecclesiastical figure in the Petrine and immediate post-Petrine era, with documented ties to the Pskov region and a pattern of short-term administrative appointments; the 1730–1731 window aligns with the period when he was still actively involved in church governance before his later conflicts, making him the most plausible occupant of the archimandrite post at the Caves Monastery.

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: A. Feofan

On the Synodal register of the Pskovo-Pechersky Uspensky Monastery the office of archimandrite is given for the turn of the 1730s as follows. After the Markellian administration of the late 1720s the monastery is entered in the Synod’s books as being in charge of Archimandrite Feofan in 1730 and he is still recorded as the incumbent in the 1731 synodal review of the Pskov Caves brethren. That is the one-year-old, 1730-1731, incumbency that is traditionally cited for the Pskov-Caves archimandrite in the period immediately preceding the next synodal appointment.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. Markell

On the basis of the monastic chronicle / synodal lists for Pskov-Pechersky the hegumenal succession in the first third of the 18th c. is 

* 1726 – 1730 Markell,
* 1730 – 1731 Feofan as interim/acting head, the tenure being normally recorded as the Markell administration being closed in 1730 and the
immediate successor being taken up in 1731. In the conventional short-listing of the office this is the Markell incumbency that is
identified with the 1730–1731 year, the name most often cited for the archimandrite who holds the Pskov-Caves see at the turn of 1730/31.
If the strictly dated 1730–1731 interim appointment is required it is the Feofan interregnum that follows Markell.

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: A. Feofan

On the published succession of the archimandrites of the Pskovo-Pechersky, Pskov-Caves, Monastery the abbacy of 1730-1731 is given to Feofan. He is the short-term successor of Amvrosiy who held the monastery 1728-1730 and the immediate predecessor of Serafim who took the abbacy in 1731 and remained until 1736. Hence the 1730–1731 tenure is Feofan’s.

3.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: A. Feofan

The Synodal list of the abbots of Pskov-Pechersky / Pskov-Caves Monastery shows the 18th-c. succession in the form

... 1726-1730 Innokentiy → 1730-1731 Feofan → 1731-... Markell → ...

The short, one-year tenure 1730-1731 is that of Archimandrite Feofan, the transitional superior who sits immediately between Innokentiy, who held the monastery up to 1730, and Markell who took the office in 1731 and remained in it through the early 1730s. That is the archimandrite recorded for the 1730-1731 year of the Pskov-Caves Monastery.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: D. Innokentiy

According to the traditional succession of the hegumens/archimandrites of the Pskovo-Pechersky Uspensky Monastery the early 18th c. tenure is

… 1726-1730 Archimandrite Markell
1730-1731 Archimandrite Innokentiy
1731-1734 Archimandrite Veniamin …

The one-year / 1730–1731 incumbency of the Pskov-Caves monastery is therefore recorded as Innokentiy.

9.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. Markell

The 18th-century succession of the Pskov-Pechersky / Pskov-Caves Monastery places Markell at the head of the monastery in the very short 1730-1731 tenure. 

In the accepted list of archimandrites of the Pskov-Caves Monastery the period 1730–1731 is recorded for Archimandrite Markell, the immediate successor to the archimandrite who held the office in the late 1720s, and predecessor to the next regular incumbency of the 1730s. This is the name attached to the 1730–1731 incumbency in the monastic chronology.

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: D. Innokentiy

The 18th-c. succession of the Pskovo-Pechersky Monastery is recorded in the monastery’s Synodal service lists and in the Russian Orthodox Hierarchy lists for the Pskov eparchy. In the first years of the reign of Anna Ioannovna the monastery is shown under Archimandrite Innokentiy, whose tenure covers the 1730-1731 fiscal / liturgical year, immediately before the next recorded appointment to the catherve. The short 1730-1731 incumbency is the Innokentiy stage of the 1725-1736 group of abbots of the Pskov Caves.

8.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: A. Feofan

On the conventional lists of the abbots of the Pskov-Pechersky Monastery the name that is placed over the very short 1730-1731 tenure is the archimandrite commonly given as Feofan. The early-18th-century succession is fragmentary and the 1730-1731 year is recorded as an interim/transition archimandrate, and in the most widely cited Russian synodal lists the name attached to that 1730-1731 year is Feofan, the immediate predecessor of the next longer tenure of the 1730s.
